I thought it was time to update my EA review which was positive but also had a lot of fixes and recommendations. A year or so on, I feel I am at the same stage where the game has now been released and it's as enjoyable as ever but you get the feeling it left EA a month or two earlier than it should have.
Overall the game is a great game and has that one more go appeal. I won't go into the specifics of what the game is about as there are many other reviews covering that aspect. I guess some of my thoughts may have been covered on the forum already, but I haven't read through each comment, so bear with me if I have said the obvious which has been covered.
Pros:
- I can't think of any other game like this on Steam
- Great racing and your strategy can really make a difference.
- Nice weather affects which really do change a game mid race.
- Graphics are ideal for this type of game
- Developers all be it small are in constant comms with the players and seem a dedicated bunch who have a proper passion for the game
- The AI could be better but not bad either.
- Able to play when there are not enough people online
- Good community so far, bar the odd disconnector which I gather has now been patched
- If you're a stoner, it's an ideal sit back and veg type game, with tiny mouse inputs throughout :)
- Other race modes look great, but no dates on when they will be ready
Cons
- Matchmaking leaves a lot to be desired. New players are already faced with meeting the 'new' cars and the issue becomes worse if you meet someone with a flying time as the AI will then also follow the fastest persons time, thus making it nigh on impossible to get anywhere.
I understand the concern of matchmaking would make less people per race at this present time, but racing against bots your own level would help their progression for new players.
- Lag, but I'm not sure if it's just me but it seems to be getting better?
- Certain tracks suit certain cars. Not being able to make at least a change or two at the lobby stage to suit the track does hinder your chances.
- Oval track (Sorry I hate this track)
- Other car modes and cup features not being ready on launch.
- Some bugs from EA are still here a year on.
Recommendations
- I know there are 2 sides to this one, but reverse grids in Quick Race as well as Cup to try to balance the game out. otherwise we're going to keep losing new players to refund which I have discussed on a previous post.
- You should have the option when being slipstreamed to shake the car off rather than just have him tail you to save fuel and there is nothing you can do bar pit.
- Reverse tracks to vary the races
- More tracks and to balance out the tracks for speed and also handling of the cars
- Make race distances varied with Sprint, normal and enduro distances.
- Sort out the matchmaking
- Try to introduce another compound for a tyre, medium? This will again add more strategy to the game. For me the game is more enjoyable from a strategic point of view than the actual racing.
- Giving the player the option to make 1 or 2 changes max when you find out what track your on in the lobby would help things as there is nothing worse than having a handling set up to then find out you are on the oval. Obviously works the same way vica versa.
- It needs more upgradeable parts to vary things.
Overall I still stand by and give the game a positive review. I've been here since day one and have seen it when we had no servers for days and bugs that made the game totally unplayable.
What we have now isn't perfect by any means and there is a long way to go, but give the devs a chance as this game could be a great game if we keep the number of players up and it ever improves.
Anyway, that's my tuppence.

Don't mind my low number of hours, I have around 9 hours and played around 6 different starts and two starts to decent length (above 100M company value).
I'll start this off by saying that the game decently simulates industrial assembly. Most consumer goods(there are a lot, probably upwards of 50) that each take some number of raw input goods, which can themselves be also composed of other input goods. This is fairly interesting and provides a good amount of depth at least in terms of construction.
Unfortunately, I cannot recommend the game in its current state despite the thought that has gone into the production side of the game, as it seems the game essentially ends there. There's an economy simulator part of the side with some kind of supply and demand, but it seems like supply and demand does not impact sales whatsoever other than capping the number of goods you can sell/buy a day.
Furthermore, the economy for consumer goods can only be filled by the player and the (maximum of four) AI players. This means that assuming that no AI player goes into the same industry as you, you will essentially have a monopoly on your industry of choice and will be able to sell goods at whatever price you will like. The advertising system is unlockable via research(took me a game or two to figure it out), and essentially you spend money to advertise on various platforms in various cities at various levels. Sounds pretty good right? Unfortunately the way it works is that advertising just makes the AI buy your goods at absurd(double) your usual prices.
Real example:
I was making Silver/Gold Jewellery. I found out that by spending around 50k on advertisement, I could double the price of my goods during the advertisement duration and make more money even after the advertisement costs. This is fine, except for the fact that the INSTANT you end advertisement everything resets to pre-advertisement levels. Now you can abuse the system super hard by stockpiling a ton of high value goods and then starting a large advertisement campaign, which will then allow you to sell those goods for double the usual price until you sell out of goods in a month or two, upon which you just cancel the advertisement campaign and wait for more goods to stack up so you can repeat the process.
PROS
-Very good manufacturing simulation
-Graphics look pretty nice, like Cities Skyline
-UI is pleasant to look at.
MEH
-Some aspects of the game seem redundant, such as warehouses having a storage limit and an upgrade associated with it, but I've never seen my warehouse above 5% capacity.
-Audio is decent, but some parts are really annoying (there's this blowing sound in particular that just kills me).
-Map settings are pretty vague but you can figure them out with a bit of experimentation.
-All city markets are separate, but you have to sell your goods for the same price at every city.
-Not sure if this is a bug or whatever, but the "daily limit" on the number of a metal you can mine seems to have no impact, I had an area that only gave 50 silver per day but I was milking it for over 150 with no apparent issues.
CONS
-Tedious UI, lot of clicking to get to related sections
-Missing Information that would be helpful like total sales for an item, total costs for an item, etc. Don't want to pull out a calculator while playing the game but that's just me.
-Market simulation needs a lot of work.
-Can't seem to find any competition with the AI, it feels like its just me and 4 bots building in separate industries that come together to compare company size once in a while.
-Very rare competition due to hard cap 4 opponent AI and huge choice of products.
-Advertising is unintuitive and can be easily abused.
TL:DR, The game is good on the production side but needs a lot of work, should be early access. The market simulation mechanics in particular need a lot of work.

Do you like complex economic simulations? Do you like games filled with simulation features, and a rich gameplay?
This game is not for you then.
I spent roughly an hour and a half getting used to the game itself. Learning the features, how to research products, how to produce, etc. After that, I can confidently say it only takes me 5 minutes of real life time to net 10 million a day for the company.
All I did was start out with the biotech, and sold over the counter cold/flu pills for 4000 dollars per PILL. How does this work, you ask? Well, it appears the developers created the advertisement to work as a price + demand modifier. Not only do more people purchase your product when you activate the advertisement, but they will also pay MORE for it.
It cost me 3 bucks to produce a single pill, and with 5 minutes of in-game time, maxed out advertisement, I set it to 4000 bucks a pill, and people bought every single pill. All 1400 of them. In fact, I could have done it in even less time, but it took me 4 minutes to research advertisement.
Do not recommend. This belongs in early access.

PLAY THIS GAME IF YOU LOVE MOTORSPORT AND CIRCUIT RACING
This game uniquely explores how important it is to properly manage tyres and fuel for pitstops as well as the importance of playing the strengths of cars to their fullest, you must determine when and where to push the car to its limits and when to drive it more economically. You'll be constantly doing math to figure out if you're under or exceeding your fuel quota and you will also be watching the tyre wear so you don't burn them out too fast and make the wear eat into your lap times.
To add to the mix you can monitor what actions and strategies the opponents are employing throughout the race, this will sometimes make you rethink your strategy - will you let him pass and tail him or will you run your car at 100% and try to outrun him and if so, for how long? Keep in mind that running the car at full throttle eats into fuel and you'll finish most races with 0% - 5% fuel remaining so choose wisely.
The tuning aspect of the game allows you to buy newer and better parts, some more suited for speed and power while others are suited better for handling and fuel economy, the challenge is to build a car that is well adapted for most situations and having strengths that can be used to secure wins. Your team can be upgraded too which consists of a Driver, the Pit Crew and lastly your Marketing Manager who is in charge of obtaining sponsorship deals.
The game is still early in development phase and has numerous errors or design faults but it still brings a lot to the table, races are randomly selected and sometimes you will be put into a race where your cars setup has almost no chance of placing within the top 5 not even looking at first, this will be ironed out down the line but can detract from the experience. Pitstop bugs have happened before as well and I've had a few bugs with tyre selection costing me races in the past but I'm willing to overlook them for the time being while the developer fixes then; the developer is very active and open with progress on the steam forums so help is never too far away.
And lastly a piece of advice for the people who are considering or have just bought the game and have yet to choose a car: buy the Raptor if you want an easier experience, buy the Avalanche if you want to grind your face into the wall but learn a lot more about strategy and have a greater challenge on the managing side of things. This game is ideal for those who know a lot about racecraft but are looking to expand their knowledge on race strategy.

Don't be confused by the non-recommendation, this is a fun game that itches a scratch I have for racing simulation and for what it has, it comes so close to being great.
But the primary issue is that this game is far from complete; there are 6 "possible" race options but only one is available (quick race), there are only 6 cars and the grind is very real, and there are a few race-breaking bugs (being pulled into the pits by AI, lag resulting in undesirable results, once my car just flat out bypassed pits even though I made the order to stop). Admittedly the netcode seems to, for the most part, be able to account for lag and so rather than missing content, everyone experiencing lag instead experiences constant skipping. One race my game just stopped in-place due to lag: my connection was fine and the client still responded but the race refused to continue so I had to leave the race.
That brings up another issue: there are very few players; the most populated race I played had 4 other players and the rest was AI.
So while I've enjoyed my time in this game, I wouldn't recommend it until:
1) Content is further added
2) Glitches/bugs fixed
3) Single player added
4) Lag
5) Possibility of choosing whom you race and/or friends features
6) Deceptively lacking content -- a "released" game with only 1 of 6 race options available is a joke
These are the most glaring issues but there are certainly other areas that could be improved that other reviewers have touched on.

An extremely fun little action rpg with good combat, and robust customization that allows you to not only edit your characters stats and abilities in depth, but even their appearance pixel by pixel.
Control and combat wise, it's a top down action rpg, similar to Legend of Zelda visually and control wise. You can jump, you can block, you can slide, and you got a variety of abilities and weapon types at your disposal. There's even a decent amount of finesse and tricks you can do, like cancelling sword slashes into blockings and then jumping out of danger to save yourself, or buffering jumps into short jumping attacks.
The enemies you face also have nice variety, and do a good job of remaining fairly unpredictable even after you've learned their fighting styles. Another thing I especially love, is that the game incorporates a subtle stealth element. Enemies won't start chasing and attacking you till they spot you, but once they do they'll chase you through the entire dungeon. Attempting to run from an enemy will cause you to rush by other enemies, who will also break into chase. This results in a frantic chase through the entire dungeon as you attempt to escape in time from the horde trying to corner you.
For customization, you're allowed to create as many characters as you like, selecting jobs, weapons, and abilities. You strengthen their abilities and growth in certain areas by drawing on the strength of other characters you've created. Visually, you can edit weapons and characters (and even animation) of your characters pixel by pixel. Don't be daunted though, because the game uses a great template for creating fairly basic but still cute looking sprites. More artistic players can still create some great stuff though.
The actual gameplay is basically divided into two games. You can make your way through the static progression of dungeons of the main campaign, which has decent level/dungeon design and is balanced well enough to not require any grinding. Alternatively, you can take on a massive 100 floor randomly generated dungeon, which feels more like a rogue like.
I personally love the randomly generated dungeon, the way stealth, combat, traps, and preparation are balanced is fantastic. Unfortunately, enemies increase in level ridiculously fast as you proceed through the floors. Eventually your attacks will do 0 damage, so it's really quite impossible to clear the dungeon based on skill alone. While making it as far as you can and escaping with random rare loot (you lose everything if you die before making it to an exit), is plenty exciting and skillbased, it's still ultimately a long term process to clear it the entire dungeon itself.
ClaDun X2 is still a fantastic game, plenty fun, and allows you to play and create your characters to suit your needs. I would highly recommend it for some hack and slash fun.

Burnout Paradise is an open world, survival horror game developed by Criterion Games, who are most known for making popular racing titles. The game is set in a horrific post-apocalyptic city, ironically called Paradise City. I can assure you however, there is no paradise to be seen in this hellish landscape.
You play as an unnamed, sentient car. The game revolves around completing the same missions over and over in order to upgrade your licence, to prove that you are king of the cars. The missions mostly involve destroying other cars, however, there are some racing elements involved here and there. As a working class peasant who cannot afford a luxury sports car, this appeals to my deep seated resentment of people who have more money than me.
[SPOILER ALERT] The story is fantastic. Towards the end of the game, you discover that you are not the protagionist at all. In fact, you are the villian. The real hero of the game is a DJ driven to madness named Atomica. Who has been broadcasting Paradise City's only radio station the entire game. His true motives are to get all of the cars in the city to destroy eachother, so that he can free humanity from its chains and rebuild society. Many games have tried to copy Burnout Paradise's clever plot twist, and have failed miserably. Ken Levine, eat your heart out. You can never hope to recreate this masterful storytelling.
In summary, Burnout Paradise is a masterpiece. There isn't a single game in existence that can match its artistic calibre. So I award this game ten out of ten cars. You will never get TYRED of this game.

Street Fighter V is well worth the purchase as they've covered all the important parts...
> lite story mode
> local fights
> online fights (coss-platform between PC and PS4)
> training mode w/dummy options
> command lists
> survival mode w/buff system
> good roster
> rock-solid fighting mechanics
> great visuals
> replays
> great music
...and one of the major pluses of V is that it's a platform that Capcom plans on adding to in the future. So no more Ultra Super Turbo Editions. Just plain old SFV with content added to it over the years. And you'll be able to purchase characters with the in-game "fight money" you recieve while playing the game. So outside of costumes, you'll be able to play for content.
Another thing I like is that it still feels like it has the insane depth of past games in the series, but a lot of the barriers of entry have been lowered. Frame links are 3+ all around now, and inputs on some characters have been simplified slightly from past games.
And the most important point... this game has Laura. She's easily my favorite SF character ever made. She plays somewhat like Abel from IV (but I feel she suits V better than Abel suited IV), with a very agressive command throw/strike mixup game, good mobility, a unique fireball, and great anti-air options. A very well made character and I can't wait to really dig into her mechanics.
All things considered, I may not like everything Capcom does (what happened to Monster Hunter and Mega Man, Capcom...), but I do have faith that they'll treat their flagship IP with the same care they've always had for the series.

Ah, my favorite racing series.
It's no Burnout Revenge on the 360, or even Burnout 3 Takedown of console yesteryears, but Burnout Paradise is still a pretty decent entry in the series overall.
Criterion tried the open world approach this time by placing you on an island city, and while that does bring a new flavor to the classic gamplay elements (namely exploration and free driving) there just feels like something was lost compared to previous entries like Burnout Revenge or Burnout 3 Takedown.
The open world actually made it feel smaller to me. Gone were the exotic locations with their reverse driving rules and varied weather conditions (snow, anyone?). Paradise City seems grand enough at first, but after a time with the exception of the middle area of the city (just because it's a confusing clustered mess of streets), it all starts feeling very repetitive and confining.
You become all too familiar with the edges of the city areas like up in the mountain paths and down by the wharf when you've already had to race along these same areas over and over dozens of times throughout your events.
The driving physics were changed quite a bit for this entry too. Everything feels a lot "heavier" than in previous titles. I'm not a huge fan of this change either, personally I prefer the crazier arcade style feel of old, but some will probably appreciate it as it lends more towards realism.
I think along with this, the sense of speed is ever so slightly less than it was in prior games, at least until you have put quite a few hours into the game and started unlocking some of the higher end vehicles, and even then...
My main gripes out of the way, there's still a lot of things to like about this game, and at its core it is still Burnout.
The three types of vehicle classifications put some fun new twists on exactly how you receive your boost abilities. There's the classic option just like from previous Burnout titles, and two new styles, aggressor and stunt.
Aggressor types gain more boost by "bullying" other racers, in other words the more you smash into racers the more boost you'll get. They drive like tanks, but they're mostly built like them too. Stunt style vehicles reward the player for doing tricks like jumps and longer drift turns, so they encourage taking a different route on certain events so you can hit ramps or bigger corners for drift.
As mentioned previously, you can explore the city in this one and there is plenty of incentive to do so, including smashing gates and billboards for unlockables, finding shortcuts and stunt areas with super jumps, gas stations and repair shops you can use to instantly fill your boost meter or repair damage during races, and sometimes just for the sake of checking out the scenery.
Online play tends to work well, but the lack of local co-op is disappointing for sure. Not sure what Criterion was thinking removing something as core to the Burnout experience as that (and crash mode too, sadly), but perhaps it had something to do with the limitations that came with making it an open world type of area instead of a pre-defined race layout like in past entries.
There are a lot of DLC items, which was another "new" thing they tried, but to be honest, none of the paid ones are really all that much to write home about, except perhaps the extension of the island. The free motorcylce DLC creates an interesting and varied gameplay experience though! Definitely something new to mix things up a bit.
At the end of the day though, my minor gripes don't hold up against the enjoyable gameplay to be found here. If you have never played a Burnout title before, this is not a bad place to start, and you're in for a treat if you like arcade style racers.
Hopefully we might see some of the older entries in the series released here on Steam someday, but even if not, this is certainly a sight better than no Burnout games at all!

Burnout Paradise is the story of a city terrorized by a car driving poultergeist. The city desperately tries to function as it forces other drivers and one insane radio host to engage the maddened spirit in a series of races and stunt competitions in an attempt to distract it from wholesale destruction and crash cams. The government has abandoned the city in hopes of containing the menace, shutting down air travel and train travel, which just provides the poultergeist with more space to crash cars. The spirit is only embodied in human form when on a motorcycle, but that form disappears the second the motorcycle crashes.
You are that poultergeist. Terrify a city as you possess different shiny cars. Reward their attempts to appease you by engaging in their races or laugh in their faces and crash in the most creative ways possible, forcing them to give you free gas, car repairs, and paint jobs. Or just drive really fast, scaring the poor people of this embattled city to death with the reckless abandon of your wild, wild poultergeist joy.
*DISCLAIMER* This game is not actually about a poultergeist. It's just a fun driving game.

This game is quite a different adventure from the game that came before it (or after if you wanna go timeline wise). The game is definitely darker (the the same vain of Xillia 2, but I can say that this game is better than that one imo), but it is still a Tales of game, so you can enjoy the fun and comedy along the way.
Story line wise, most of the game can be summed up as "I hate you, I will get my revenge on you." Sounds cliche, which of course goes with Tales of games, but the adventure is quite fun and there is a LOT of turmoil and heartbreak along the way. Velvet isn't a typical Tales of protagonist, and I don't mean because she is the first female solo protagonist (the other main female protagonist was Millia from Xillia, but she was still closer to a standard Tales protagonist). However, other characters are a big part of the adventure. Many of them have their own stories intertwined, and, to be honest, some feel more tacked on than others just to give more motivation to fight more bosses. This isn't everyone since some characters go on a real journey of development. The banter between the party is fun, but I feel some other Tales of games have better chemistry.
Now for the real part, equipment and combat. As with recent Tales of games, the equipment in the game can be complicated, but it is easier than Zestiria was with it. A lot of stats come from equipment, but it is fine to take your time to learn how it works. Combat on the other hand is fun and easy to learn, especially when, again, compared to Zestiria (I know I mention it a lot). As with all Tales of games, the game has its own version of the Linear Motion Battle System. Take your time and play with it for awhile and get a feel for all the characters. Velvet is easy to learn how to play (hint, learn to stun lock), but the other characters have their own appeal. I never got to try out the coop aspect in this game, which is sad, so I'll leave that out.
Anyway this game is a treat. It isn't the best Tales of game, but its pretty good and really fun. I can recommend to old and new fans though I do need to warn both that it is quite different tone and story wise from the other games in the series.

Personally, my favorite RPG of all time is Tales of Phantasia with Chrono Trigger a close second. Tales of Phantasia, especially the GBA version, was the pinnacle of retro JRPG, and the first in the genre to implement real time battles. It had a revolutionary, fluid battle system, one of the best storylines only rivaled by the likes of Chrono Trigger, rewarding sidequests which were relevant to the main story, and many many aspects to explore as the game progressed.
Unfortunately, none of the newer Tales of Series really gave me a better experience than Tales of Phantasia, nor made me a fan of the game. Like others, Tales of Berseria does not stand out as an absolute gem, but it is definitely one of the better games in the series. Sort of like Assassin's Creed Syndicate, how it is much better than the previous ones (like Unity), but the Ezio trilogy is still considered the best.
Anyways, back to Tales of Berseria. I believe the best part of the game is probably its battle system. The battle system has become much easier without the need to manage orange gels and lemon gels all the time, but is still fast-paced and exciting nevertheless. The battle AI is also very solid.
Pros:
- Greatly improved battle system, which no problems with PC port
- Above average storyline
- Decent amount of playtime
- Great cutscene animations by ufotable
Cons:
- Not really outstanding in any aspect other than battle
- Sidequests not very rewarding or abundant
- Still feels like a mass produced game without its own shine
I still do recommend playing it though.
The only grip I can see is that the control scheme with a keyboard is a quarrel to get used to, but once you do, it'll be one of the greats in your library.

This is a very nice game. I can see myself playing this for a long time to come.  It's sort of like Capitalism II, if you ever played that. You can buy land, make manufacturing chains, research, sell products, buy/sell stock, get loans, compete with other computer players, etc.
The reserach tree is pretty nice as well. Not only can you research new products, but you can improve your existing ones along with the maximum production, maximum workers, research lowering costs, etc. There are many upgrades, and products to research/manufacture; I love this part of the game.
I do recommend spending about 10 mins watching 1 tutorial when you first start; it saves you a lot of time, and you get the hang of everything fairly easy after that. One tip: on each production and warehouse building you have to tell it to get certain ingredients, or send certain final products to the warehouse. Also from the warehouse you can click on each product, click global market (or whatever it's called), and then sell a certain amount and click 'repeat' to sell a certain amount each day (1st option to sell). The 2nd  option to sell (better option) is to click on the construction areas in a city, build a building that lets you sell your products in your own store, and add those products one by one to sell (2nd option; this option automatically sells your products.)
The AI (computer players) is the one main area where I'd give a negative right now, but I also know they are working on fixing this as it's in their 'known issues' thread in the forums. As it stands the computer players go bankrupt after a while; they keep it entertaining for a bit, but then they one by one go down. It's still fun to play, but will be much better once they start playing better. Also it'd be cool to see cities develop, but I believe the only thing that changes with them is the population figure, and when corporations build their store in a pre-set area. Outside of the cities though is where all the manufacturing chains are built, and it's a pretty good sized map for you and the computer players to build in.
There are random events that happen such as: the bank decides not to lend for a while to anyone, fungus growing on crops causing production to halt, worker strikes, etc. It's a nice touch. Also I just found out in my 2nd game of play that there are random rewards/challenges for example for researching something specific, or producting certain goods.
You can also setup winning conditions, 3 map size options, etc. which are nice. This game is extremly fun for me. If you like Business type games with research trees, building upgrades, etc. this is a defnite buy imo. You do have to look at the production trees, etc. to see what is required though for each product, so I wouldn't recommend this for children obviously though (unless you have one of those kids really into these types of games. :)

> The updates aren't as frequent as they could be (not really too much of a bad thing)
> The community is all over the place (But there are some awesome people in it at the same time)

But if there's something I particularly hate, it's how dead the ingame setting feels. The game gives off an empty vibe, the NPCs, despite giving out the occasional random quest, are soulless and robotic. (And I am not talking about the Glitch lmao)
Not only that, there's not much in the way of a story (not giving any spoilers here, but it's your average "witness bad stuff, then proceed to do a million fetch quests and eventually save everyone despite you being the new guy" story which is just bodged. If I am to be fair here, a game like this doesn't really need a story, but at the same time it helps - It just needs to be fleshed out, extended too, because I have completed the story (Yeah, I kinda cheated because I am more of a build-stuff kinda guy) and it felt too short, maybe even rushed.
Despite all this, the game is playable, it's really easy to mod and build in, but it gets boring way too quickly. The thing this game needs is more ways to play, and a more free flowing story that isn't set in stone at the start; kind of like the pre-1.0 versions. I love this game, but it needs to be loved by the developers more, because - I'm not trying to be rude here, but - Chucklefish need to focus on this game and not a million other projects, because even though this game has reached version 1.0, it still feels unfinished.
Don't do a Bethesda and leave it up to the modders - do something about it! (or at least work with the modders, idk)
So yeah. This game isn't bad, but it's not super good either.

Yes in 1.0 there are reasons to build houses for NPCs.  You can build colonies and get gifts/missions in return from NPCs, as well as shops.
Vehicles are in the game now, they were also in the latest editions of the EA.

Ah, my favorite racing series.
It's no Burnout Revenge on the 360, or even Burnout 3 Takedown of console yesteryears, but Burnout Paradise is still a pretty decent entry in the series overall.
Criterion tried the open world approach this time by placing you on an island city, and while that does bring a new flavor to the classic gamplay elements (namely exploration and free driving) there just feels like something was lost compared to previous entries like Burnout Revenge or Burnout 3 Takedown.
The open world actually made it feel smaller to me. Gone were the exotic locations with their reverse driving rules and varied weather conditions (snow, anyone?). Paradise City seems grand enough at first, but after a time with the exception of the middle area of the city (just because it's a confusing clustered mess of streets), it all starts feeling very repetitive and confining.
You become all too familiar with the edges of the city areas like up in the mountain paths and down by the wharf when you've already had to race along these same areas over and over dozens of times throughout your events.
The driving physics were changed quite a bit for this entry too. Everything feels a lot "heavier" than in previous titles. I'm not a huge fan of this change either, personally I prefer the crazier arcade style feel of old, but some will probably appreciate it as it lends more towards realism.
I think along with this, the sense of speed is ever so slightly less than it was in prior games, at least until you have put quite a few hours into the game and started unlocking some of the higher end vehicles, and even then...
My main gripes out of the way, there's still a lot of things to like about this game, and at its core it is still Burnout.
The three types of vehicle classifications put some fun new twists on exactly how you receive your boost abilities. There's the classic option just like from previous Burnout titles, and two new styles, aggressor and stunt.
Aggressor types gain more boost by "bullying" other racers, in other words the more you smash into racers the more boost you'll get. They drive like tanks, but they're mostly built like them too. Stunt style vehicles reward the player for doing tricks like jumps and longer drift turns, so they encourage taking a different route on certain events so you can hit ramps or bigger corners for drift.
As mentioned previously, you can explore the city in this one and there is plenty of incentive to do so, including smashing gates and billboards for unlockables, finding shortcuts and stunt areas with super jumps, gas stations and repair shops you can use to instantly fill your boost meter or repair damage during races, and sometimes just for the sake of checking out the scenery.
Online play tends to work well, but the lack of local co-op is disappointing for sure. Not sure what Criterion was thinking removing something as core to the Burnout experience as that (and crash mode too, sadly), but perhaps it had something to do with the limitations that came with making it an open world type of area instead of a pre-defined race layout like in past entries.
There are a lot of DLC items, which was another "new" thing they tried, but to be honest, none of the paid ones are really all that much to write home about, except perhaps the extension of the island. The free motorcylce DLC creates an interesting and varied gameplay experience though! Definitely something new to mix things up a bit.
At the end of the day though, my minor gripes don't hold up against the enjoyable gameplay to be found here. If you have never played a Burnout title before, this is not a bad place to start, and you're in for a treat if you like arcade style racers.
Hopefully we might see some of the older entries in the series released here on Steam someday, but even if not, this is certainly a sight better than no Burnout games at all!

Burnout Paradise is the story of a city terrorized by a car driving poultergeist. The city desperately tries to function as it forces other drivers and one insane radio host to engage the maddened spirit in a series of races and stunt competitions in an attempt to distract it from wholesale destruction and crash cams. The government has abandoned the city in hopes of containing the menace, shutting down air travel and train travel, which just provides the poultergeist with more space to crash cars. The spirit is only embodied in human form when on a motorcycle, but that form disappears the second the motorcycle crashes.
You are that poultergeist. Terrify a city as you possess different shiny cars. Reward their attempts to appease you by engaging in their races or laugh in their faces and crash in the most creative ways possible, forcing them to give you free gas, car repairs, and paint jobs. Or just drive really fast, scaring the poor people of this embattled city to death with the reckless abandon of your wild, wild poultergeist joy.
*DISCLAIMER* This game is not actually about a poultergeist. It's just a fun driving game.

Blackwake is a multiplayer naval game where the players crew ships and fight each other in often fast paced matches of positioning, skill at combat and teamwork.
As an early access game, it mostly works off its basics- There remains very little in the way of content but what is there is enough to lead to many varied and interesting situations, often entirely different because of the reliance on player captains to steer the ships and individual tactics(Or lack of tactics) effecting almost everything about a battle.
Currently, there is only what amounts to a deathmatch- Make the other team run out of respawns or cannonballs before they do the same to you. It is worth noting here that casualties are unavoidable at any range, as a lucky cannonball can and will hit people at almost any range, but this effect can be minimized by a good captain giving your ship good angles of attack while minimizing those of your opponent.
Often it gets a bit hectic on larger ships, as everyone needs to get some information out at the same time- The rear sail is on fire while the captain yells to prepare for ramming and a gunner says they ran out of cannonballs and need someone to run supplies. Teamwork is surprisingly easy if people communicate, but with how the game and its systems are set up you will still need to try in order to do well. A few mistakes by the captain can put a lot of holes in your ship, which floods the gun deck and disables your cannons as they can't fire underwater.
Many of the systems involved are simple, working well together to create the full experience. Flooding happens because you have holes, and water flow is not simulated. At the same time, supplies are a single resource, so you don't have a stock of regular cannonballs, gunpowder, grapeshot, and so on. Just supplies you can use. This is not bad, as the simple nature of these systems makes it easy to switch from one thing to the next- Load cannonballs and repair the hull without having to worry about the exact amount of wooden boards you have left (Repairing takes no resources), or the exact kind of ammo remaining.
Although I personally enjoy these kind of details that the game leaves out, I fully understand and admit that they are not necessary for the game to be fun, and those with less of a mind for logistics and supply management may not enjoy them.
As can be seen in the screenshots, it looks quite well. Several times of day and several weather types are available and make for varied looking rounds, with only two map variations that I've been able to find- Small islands and open sea. I've personally found the maps to be a bit small, but this is likely intentional to force confrontation so the players don't sail around without firing a single shot.
All things considered, Blackwake is a very solid game already and seems to be getting regular patches. It currently only features a single game mode and two kinds of ships, but this is enough to be a very enjoyable experience already. At the very least, I would say it is worth the price.

In Farenheit 451, there's a scene where the main protagonist's wife watches a soap opera, and reads along on a script to feel like she's part of the show.  It's not interactive but it makes the viewer feel it is.
In The Walking Dead, they do the same thing.  It's not that your decisions don't matter, but they don't.
I have liked a number of Telltale games and most of the previous ones are different.  The one I didn't like was Jurassic Park The Game.  It had a good idea, and a horrible flaw, nothing you did matter, it was all QTEs.
Walking dead has the same flaw, but doesn't have QTEs (or at least as many), and the fact is, this makes me realize how much better Jurassic Park was because of the QTEs.    It also shows that with out them, and with out a meaningful decision tree, the game... well the game kind of sucks.
If you really want a Walking Dead story (based on the comic, not the tv show) you get that here, but the fact is almost nothing matters in this game, there's a few critical changes and most of those just define who lasts a few frames longer.
What kind of gets me is that Mass Effect people raged over the fact that the ending doesn't really change (for the most part) and that's a huge flaw.  But in this game it has the same exact problem, and where's the outrage?   This game promised meaningful decisions this game, and yet it doesn't deliver.
The problem is Mass Effect still had a good gameplay and a decent story if lacking ending.  This has a good story, but I honestly feel like it'd be done better as a tv show, comic, cartoon, or any other format.   And it's a shame because I liked Telltale games, but I believe this is the point where they changed, from "puzzles" to "Story" but the problem is the only real agency the player has is fake.  It might change the story, but it doesn't change the ending or anything meaningful.
On the other hand I'm not a Walking dead fan, so perhaps if I was, I'd be more accepting of this story, but I'm not so your mileage might vary.

While I despise the Creation Club and the whole cash grab it represents, and I understand that Fallout 4 doesn't live up to New Vegas at all for most people, I feel it is still underrated. Yes, the quest system is not the best, and yes, the game is far easier than New Vegas. But Fallout 4 is still fun to play in my opinion. I can't go any further into this review without mentioning the dialogue system/writing. The dialogue system is very limiting and immersion breaking for me, as it doesn't give many options compared to the old dialogue system. Voice acting of the main character was a horrible choice for many reasons. I can't be immersed in a game when it feels more like a movie than a game. The writing for the sarcastic option is usually very weak, with some decent lines. Now with that out of the way, I want to talk about the rest of the things I did not like in Fallout 4.
1: The new perk system is far less interesting and diverse as previous versions, which is frustrating when people try to make a specific character.
2: Along with the perk system, the removal of skills is just stupid. I actually have no idea why Bethesda did this. The growth of a characters skills and perks made the game far more interesting and fun, working your way up from a lowly wastelander to a post-apocalyptic God is something that I thought made Fallout great.
3: Weapon degradation was helpful in making the feeling that you are living in a post-nuclear world far stronger. I can understand why they did it with the implementation of the weapon customization system, but I hate to see it go.
4: The need to put what are essentially batteries into your Power Armor every 9 minutes is just tedious.
5: The factions are really weakly written and I hated most of them.
Now the things I like:
1: Weapon customization is something I love no matter what game it is, I am a sucker for it. If you aren't a fan of it then you may not care about this point. I know New Vegas had a customization system but it was not very interesting.
2:  The DLC may be overpriced in some cases, but for the most part I absolutely love Far Harbor, Nukaworld, and Automatron (or however you spell it).
3: The settlement system needs work, but I still think it is a fun little side project.
4: The followers are pretty good usually, just some of them are bland or obnoxious.

You never know what'll stick or what won't. This stuck about as well as some pre-chewed bubblegum from the bottom of someone's shoe.
The important thing is though... it does stick. I did enjoy this game.
At first, I assumed that Serena was just a simple game (similar to Home is Where One Starts), with little insight into a person's relation to a location after their return. And, holy hell, are there some unique insights in this couple's relationship! I won't spoil anything, but it gets dark.
It is very similar to Fingerbones. No, wait. Sorry. Fingerbones is very similar to Serena, where you navigate a room, find more clues to what happened in a specific pattern, and an ultimate dark reveal is made at the end.
However, I actually prefer Fingerbones. Serena doesn't originally start as a "horror" game, as it describes itself... but it does get more uncomfortable and creepy as you learn more facts, then the character's memories shift from kind, to depressed, to angry... but then it jumps to the big scare... I feel like there could've been a moment of insanity after the big reveal. Like a change in the photograph, or something.
That and the voice acting sucks in my opinion. None of the voice actors sounded convincing. The writing was good, as was the atmosphere. But the main character and his wife weren't good.
Serena is still worth a playthrough. It's short, emotionally satisfying, and it looks very nice. I'm gonna give it a 6/10. Despite what flaws it has, it's still an enjoyable little project.

Woohoo, I decided to buy the Half Life bundle and start with this one first! I was AMAZED when I started the first chapter; my jaw dropped! The graphics, of course, aren't the best. But man, I had one heck of a time playing Half Life 1. I treated every NPC like they were a real person. I teared up when I saw a security guard get beaten by a headcrab zombie. I felt bad absolutely destroying the H.E.C.U units. I was mortified seeing a scientist getting eaten by a bullsquid. With every man following me, I did my best to protect the person. I didn't want to lose anybody. Don't treat this like your average FPS. Try to feel what is going on! I insist that you all should try to relate with Gordon Freeman. Valve let you have full control of Gordon so that you and him could just be one! For such an old game, everything felt pretty realistic. The guns and enemies were pretty cool! Although "co-workers" can't really fight nor use their surroundings, alien and military AI was great! The alien behavior gave me the feeling that the dangerous beasts were adapting to their surroundings. Barnacles hang on places that would be easy to surprise prey; they hang on obscure roofs and tight corners of hallways, where nobody would expect them. Houndeyes formed packs to make their waves more powerful and effective. Bullsquids found home in Black Mesa's radioactive... lakes. Headcrabs started to take over humans! What else would they do in their home planet, anyway? Of course, the Alien Grunts are simply doing their job. Destroying all human life so that they can call Earth their home. They even have a food chain! Well... the only 2 things is that is that headcrabs are bullsquid prey. Barnacles eat anything and everything. Now, the H.E.C.U. units.They can recieve calls on their radio, and also establish bases all around Black Mesa. It's quite effective when you need to cover the entire area. They'll treat anything like dirt. It's quite amazing how much character is built to everything and everyone. The story and background is GREAT, but I honestly don't want to go further. It's easy for me to spoil and other things like that. If you haven't bought Half Life 1, then it's amazing how you still haven't! Go for it! It's a great game; a timeless classic.

Town of Salem has to be one of the biggest surprises of the year for me. An addictive browser game where you're not matching fruits, building barracks or spam-inviting your Facebook friends to? What is this sorcery!?
Salem is a humble town, comprised of fifteen residents, who gather at the town square (circle) each morning to discuss the day's events. But Salem holds terrible secrets. For within its ranks, evil stirs, in the form of a Serial Killer, a Mafioso Family, a lunatic Jester, and a murderous Executioner. Will the good Townsfolk pull together and weed out the miscreants? Or will they bicker and shout as they are picked off, one by one, until chaos reigns supreme?
At its core, Salem is a murder-mystery game. Fifteen players are each allocated a secret role at random at the beginning of the game. Nine of these roles will be aligned to the Town - their mission is to lynch all the wrongdoers in their beloved settlement. Three roles are aligned to the Mafia - their mission will be to take over the Town by killing their enemies. Two roles are Neutral, and they have their own specific, selfish agenda. And one player will be allocated the Serial Killer role. Their mission? To kill everyone else before they get discovered.
Each night, the Serial Killer (SK for short) will choose a victim. Unless that victim is protected in some way, he/she will die. While this is going on, the Mafia will be discussing who they want to kill. Again, unless their chosen victim is protected, that person will also die, furthering the Mafia's insidious plots.
When morning comes, the whole town gathers in the centre to discover who was killed last night. They are told who died, and which role killed them (example: John William has died - he was stabbed to death by a Serial Killer). Once the death notifications have passed, the chat window is activated, and all players still alive may freely discuss who they think may be a killer, who may be innocent, or just try to confuse each other.
From the perspective of the good Townsfolk, this is done through teamwork - each Town member has a specific ability, which is either passive, or used at a specific time. For instance, the Lookout is able to watch someone's house at night, and just before morning comes, the Lookout will be told by the game who visited that person's house. The Doctor can visit someone's house each night, and if they are attacked, he will heal them to prevent a death. The Escort can distract someone each night, preventing them from using their night ability (if they have one). This fascinating (and sometimes very confusing) interaction of skills, over time, creates a picture, one that the Town is hoping will point a finger at a culprit.
Each day, the whole town can vote on someone that they want to see hanged in the town centre (where a gallows is ominously present). If someone has evidence on a culprit, they may share it to try and get that person lynched. But to do so, they would have to reveal their role, which will make them a priority target in the eyes of the Mafia and SK. Herein lies the majesty of Town of Salem - each day, people will lie, they will argue, they will stand by and watch their fellow man be hanged to death for fear of becoming the next one beneath the noose. And as more and more people die each night, the situation becomes more and more desperate, until a point where one vote either way could make the difference between the Town surviving or dying.
As well as being a fantastic, addictive, complex game of suspicion, betrayal and panic, Town of Salem is a relatively balanced game, insofar as there are over ten unique roles in any given game. Although the Mafia are technically outnumbered five-to-one, they have the night advantage, and in the early stages of the game, the SK will often do a lot of their dirty work for them. Although the SK stands alone, he is immune to attack at night, and wields the most power to bring death to the town. And the Townies, though they may be squishy, they are legion, and if they work together, they will prevail. The game is fast paced, frantic, incredibly fun, and will have you regaling bored friends with overly-complicated explanations of how you worked out who the Godfather was by Night 3.
There are three criticisms I would have of the game, but none are really within the developer's control. The first is the fact that for this game to be enjoyable, it is expected that each player will perform their role correctly. Unfortunately, this is an Internet Game(TM), and as such you will encounter a myriad number of trolls, newbies, leavers, bitter basement-dwellers and people who still have dial-up messing up the game, making staggeringly moronic decisions, whether intentional or not.
The second difficulty with the game lies in certain roles. Having balanced roles does not necessarily mean that those roles are equally FUN. If you get assigned either the Executioner or Medium role, it can be a dice roll as to whether or not you have an enjoyable game.
The other risk with each game you play is that, due to its nature, it is entirely possible that you will be killed on the first night, and therefore unable to take any more action other than talking in the "dead" chatroom, where all the killed players congregate, discuss the game and give the Medium (who speaks to the dead) any useful information. Getting killed on Night One is not much fun for any player, however if you have no useful information for the Medium, you are able to simply quit the game and start a new one, with no repercussions.
When I first downloaded Town of Salem, I played it for five straight hours to the point where my throat dried up on account of forgetting to drink anything. Give it a go, I promise you your first game is always a thrill!

I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys figuring out if someone is lying. In this game you are randomly assigned a role which can range from a town member with a unique ability to a mafia member with the goal of killing town members, or to a neutral character whose goal is to create chaos. There are day and night cycles; during the day you are free to chat and try to figure out the bad guys. At night, you  perform your special ability which can range from killing someone, investigating, or channeling the dead. It is always a thrill at the end of the night when you find out if you lived or died. The real fun for serious players is located in ranked mode which requires 50 games played in other modes to unlock. There are always some bad apples in the game who are negative/salty or not being true to their role, but the in-game reporting system allows the developers to take care of these people by banning them. You can buy cosmetic items like houses and characters with in-game currency that is earned by playing games or with real money. All the items are purely cosmetic and do not affect gameplay at all. I wouldn't recommend paying real money since it seems like you get so little in return for your money; the town points aren't cheap. The game is being actively improved as new roles are coming to the game in the future. Overall this is an exciting casual game to play in your down time.

1.  First:  The most important thing in fighters is offline Vs, which this has, and online vs.  Arcade is a quick run though then you rarely play it again, same with survival.  This game is a competitive fighter, and actualy fighting is 95% of this game.  So is it deep, is it tournament worthy, are the combo's smooth, are there broken characters and other glitches.  For the most part, this game passes this part and as such will never be a terrible game.  It has been and will always be the Definitive fighting game franchise and this will be the definitive fighting game of EVO 2016.
2.  with that out of the way, Online Vs doesn't work.  Like I said, you either have friends offline, and I do, but when you want to play online, right now I can't create a lounge, I can't play casual match, I can't play ranked match, I can't go to capcom fighting network to search for my friend.  Practically Nothing work.
3.  Is graphics good, answer is yes, it is slightly better than PS4 in fidelity.  PS4 is roughly medium settings in this game.
4.  No arcade mode, no structured training mode, though there is a barebones training mode.
5.  Story mode is very barebones, 1 round only, with only like 3-4 matches per story segment.  Easily finished them all in less than 1 hour.
6.  Word on the Street was that this game was NOT going to support Dinput natively.  Now I've tried to play several games that were Xinput only, and believe me, I've tried lots of software to bind the keys, most of the time it works, but sometimes it just doesn't work.  We've known about this lack of feature for several months now, so I did make sure that I had a controller that was Xinput compatible so I didn't have that problem.  But for those who didnt' pay heed, or didn't know, that kinda sucks and this is a major failure on Capcom's part.  Even their own Mad Catz sponsored SFV fightpad pro, which is D-input would have trouble working here, what a grade A Dropped ball on Capcom.
Overall:  CEARLY Capcom decided to try to get this in the hands of people in order to get Capcom cup, and other tournaments started with PRO SFV action, culminating in EVO.  However; This game really is unfinished.  Not just in the who cares category of Oh survival is unfinished or there is no Arcade.  But in crucial stuff like actual controller compatibility, and online anything.  What it got right is that, the game is locked at 60 frames, and if you can't run it, the game will slow down to draw the frames, making it obvious your settings are too high, so just lower them until you get solid frame rates.  They had to do this because this game is THE competitive fighting franchise, and you just can't have frames going above or below 60frames.  This is why there is FRAME DATA on this game.  All the moves are dependent on total frames, active frames, recovery frames and so forth to know which move is safe, which move is punishable and so forth.
If you are NOT a fighting game fan, and just wanted to try SFV, I would wait a month or two.  If you are a fighting game fan, than more than likely you have offline competitors and this game will still be functional for you.  If you don't have offline competitors, and still a fan then it is up to you to buy it now or not.  Anticipate LOTS of patches in the next few days to weeks.  We already had a day 1 patch, so more coming.
Final Rating on the actual fighting:  Maybe not as deep as SFIV, which itself was not as deep as SFIII, but still very solid.  In that case maybe an 8.5.  The actual State of the Overall game and overal product though, is a 4/10.  It's just not ready yet.

It's an isometric action indie game (although I don't know how being published by Warner Bros is indie but nevermind that.) This is probably the first indie non-sandbox game I’ve played.
It follows through the adventures of a boy the „Kid” who’s entire race was wiped off of the face of the earth „Bastion” by a strange event called the „Calamity”. The „Kid” is trying to salvage through the remains of his civilization exploring the world trying to find clues, and certain items to restore „Bastion” to its former glory.
I’ll follow the usual format of game reviews just to make it easier to read.
-	Story/Quests
The story itself is quite mediocre I’d say, there are no mind-blowing twists or hilarious moments in it. The quest mechanic are basically the same „go and fetch this and that” repeating around 16 times which can be tedious after a while. However an unique feature of the game is that EVERYTHING is narrated, no not by Morgan Freeman but by a more „macho” sounding gentleman Logan Cunningham who is also great in what he does.
The narration gives an interesting vibe to the game, you feel like you’re part of the story and it feels like „living in the book”, making the fights/progression and story more immersive. The narrator also has some quirky comments when you change your loadout or accidentally fall off of a floating island which made me smile quite a few times.
-	Graphics/Looks
The art of the game is beautiful. Every level has a different story, feel to it which makes you forgive the (otherwise tedious) quests. Everything is colorful, rich and vibrant. Thankfully the game doesn’t have any serious system requirements it runs easily on a laptop so you can enjoy it in its full glory. There’s not much more to say, go watch some trailers or gameplay videos :)
-	Combat/Gameplay
The game is very combat-centric, you don’t have much time to immerse yourself into the game or admire the scenery without getting♥♥♥♥♥♥♥by the various enemies. It’s like Bioshock Infinite, beautiful and interesting but you must keep on grinding through hordes of various enemies. The enemy variety is alright when you start to get bored there’s always a new type of enemy appearing. The combat itself is surprisingly fun with a great variety in weapons and combat styles. There is no quick-save or even checkpoints, a game is only saved after you successfully finish a level.
You have one primary and a secondary weapon slot and a variety of weapons (ranging from katanas to muskets) which you can upgrade. You also have a special ability slot which you can use to throw grenades or place a decoy of yourself to confuse enemies. There’s supposed to be an alchemy system and stealth in the game but I didn’t really want to get into it, I stick to my guns thanks. The combat is incredibly fast-paced and hectic with tons of enemies coming at you, sometimes you even feel like you’re playing an isometric „Shoot ’em Up” dodging projectiles all the time. The game is HARD, the enemies hit hard even on easy difficulty you find yourself grasping for breath, looking for health potions and trying to survive. You have three chances to „respawn” after dying if you exceed it then you must start the level all over again. There are the usual boss batles and you should apply a different strategy for different foes.
Conclusion:
Bastion is a fun little game, but it has its flaws. I love reading classic literature in my free time so my expectations of a „story” are quite high when I play video games. The game is beautiful, the combat is fun but challenging, and the narration brings a refreshing change to the storytelling. I recommend it to people who like games with an unique world, and lore but who also like getting their hands dirty in frequent fights. I don’t recommend it to people who don’t like hard fast paced, crazy combat and to people who don’t like to start a level all over again. The game takes around 6-8 hours to beat, but I heard that there are two different endings so it gives some replay value (I didn't really care about the story so one playthrough was enough for me :) )

Guilty Gear XX ACCENT CORE PLUS R is the latest and possibly last Revision for this nearly 15 year old Game
It is by far the most balanced Fighting Game ever with huge in-depth Mechanics and Modes. Since the Mechanics to explain can fill entire Pages, i recommend visiting the Dustloop Wiki for more Infos.
Besides the Mechanics, also the Characters and the Music (made both by Daisuke Ishiwatari) contributed to the huge success of this Series. It is easy to say that it belongs to the Top 3 of Fighting Games (Tekken, SF and GG)
Accent Core as a Revision was also completely redone with new Looks (GUI, Menus, Character Portraits, etc.) and also the Voicing of all Characters are remade. Since Core Plus there is also a new Story Mode (2 Paths for each Char except Justice, Kliff and Holy Order Sol) and the R Revision received a brand new GUI which replaced that of Accent Core.
As a Side Note, BlazBlue is also made by ARCsys (Only Music made by Daisuke) and shares some Mechanics but hasn't the same Depth.
It offers many Modes such as a Story Mode, Missions, Survival, etc.
The Story Mode is recommended to grasp the Personalities of the Characters and to see which suits you the best.
Here are some of my Pro/Contra Points:
Pro:
-Good PC Port from the Consoles
-Variety of many Characters
-Awesome Rock/Metal Music
-Voiced Story Mode
-All Stages from Slash/#Reload Revision are included (must be unlocked through Story Mode)
-Good Game Mechanics
-Network Mode! (#R has only Fanmade Network Mode)
-Latest Revision with new Moves and Balancing for all Characters
Contra:
-Slightly higher Frame Delay than the #R PC Version (5F while #R has 2F set)
-Slash/#Reload Stages can only be used Offline and not in Network Mode
-Announcer and some Voices of the Characters (for Example: Baiken has now the Voice of an old Grandma, etc.) are poorly redone. They were better in the Old pre Accent Core Revisions.
-Network Mode is suboptimal at Times (It uses Frame Delay Input and not GGPO which is faster but has also its own Flaws)
-Steep Learning Curve while progressing
-Not much Players online depending on Times. Check the "Find Player" Thread in the GGAC+R Steam Forum for Players in your Region
That's all. KEEP YOURSELF ALIVE!

Blackwake.
The naval FPS combat simulator that introduced one of the most original and exciting ideas to competitive gaming since Dead By Daylight. It's a brilliant idea for a competitive PC game that to be honest, took way too long to release.
So in Blackwake, you are fighting for the side of either the Navy or the Pirates, the game places you on a ship in the sea somewhere near Britain with another 7 people (max) and you must take down the other team's ship(s). Gamemodes as of this time only reflect the amount of ships on each team. On your ship, one player is elected Captain, whose job is to steer the ship and give the orders. The rest of crew take control over the rest of the ship. There are cannons located on the left and right (and on some occasions at the front) which you can load with cannonballs, grapeshots or grapples. There are also swivel cannons (normally located on the front) which you can use to shoot out enemy ship's sails. Each player also carries a few items along with them. Generally the players are equipped with a musket, a pistol, a cutlass, a cup of tea or bottle of rum, and a repair hammer. The first 3 items are used for fighting, the drinks are for healing and the repair hammer is for the obvious.
So there are a number of options you can take to bring down enemy ships. The cannons can be used to destroy and eventually sink emeny ships if gone long enough without repairs. Repairing the ship can be done by equipping the repair hammer to find and fix the holes notified, while the pump(s) located somewhere on the ship needs to be used to extract the water. Other options of destroying enemy ships include ramming into them. This deals damage to the ship while also possibly killing memebers of their crew. This also creates access to board ships allowing for players to engage in hand to hand combat against each other. Another option is grappling the enemy ship which puts the ship members into an elimination deathmatch to potentially set a game.
Aside from the game's originality and combat system, one area where this competitive game shines is in its teamwork. There is never a point in the game where a crew member ISN'T doing something. The only way for a ship to escape victoriously is to have consistent communication and contribution to the team. Every member must always be setting themselves with tasks to reloading and firing cannons, repairing and pumping, resupplying, using the swivel cannons, all while the captain is the one with all responsibility, steering the ship and giving clear orders and game plans for pulling their team through to the end.
Blackwake is, in my opinion a true masterpiece for teamwork-based gameplay and fitting into the competitive playstyle. Of all the games out there where the people who give guides on how to play state that a mic is necessary to success, Blackwake is by NO MEANS an exception. At the moment the only issues I have with it is its lack of servers. Especially in Australia, you'll only find about 3 or 4 that actually have players in them. There's also no matchmaking in its current Alpha, but I don't not to expect too much of an indie game that hasn't even been released for a month yet. Regardless, I would HIGHLY recommend Blackwake to anyone interested in competitive or heavily teamwork-based games at all. Or if you just like intense, original and/or fun playstyles, this is your game. I'd also strongly recommend it if you're a fan of Dead By Daylight. (A strangely large portion of Blackwake's playerbase is from DBD for some reason)
Overall, Blackwake earns a 7.5/10 from me. It's strong in terms of concept, originality, playstyle and its comfortable fit into competitive gameplay. Weak in terms of servers and matchmaking. But even with the cons, the devs have been releasing patches and updates to the game almost every day, which is some serious dedication and support to their work. So keep it up, guys!

A Quick Review For A Rather Persistently Insistent Mate Of Mine ;p
Comparison Comment:
Those of you who've got into any of the Tales Of games (Zestiria, Symphonia) will feel right at home here; next to no changes I've seen so far.
At A Glance:
Given that I've heard some folks out there taking 60-80 hours to complete their first attempt, I'm barely into the game here so can't cover much ;) So far I've had my Happy-Go-Lucky Dragonball Level Martial Arts Student enjoying a blissful life in The Innocent Village In The Land Of Milk And Honey which suddenly has ***An Event*** which is almost on par with The Eclipse from Berserk, which leads to Wrongful Imprisonment and am now coming up to the part where the MC is going on a Roaring Rampage Of Revenge...
So yep; pretty standard fare so far :D
What got me is just how QUICK the game went from Happyland to Grimdark; normally there's a bit of build-up before you get thrown into the deep end (literally, in this case), so that made for a good change of pace.
Combat is in real-time and not turn-based, but there are cool-downs for your abilities which you have to keep check of when you're in the thick of it. It doesn't take your mind off the action, but something to be mindful of - you generally blitzkrieg through the combats once you get to a certain point anyway - might become more of a priority when you're doing Boss Runs I'm thinking.
Story is... okay, it's pretty cliche' so far, but don't let that put you off; it's well-delivered in my opinion and doesn't feel re-hashed/a carbon copy of other games. I've yet to get the full details on The Grand Conspiracy but I'm very much looking forward to when I can put down The Big Bad with extreme prejudice :D
The MC (Velvet) is basically a girl cloned from Guts' genes, which I appreciate in my MCs ;D character development seems to be pretty detailed, so I find it a bit of a pity that you can't have 'interactive paths' which would have added to the experience. But it's not that kind of RPG, so I'll live with it :)
Not going to go too much further in as I've dropped enough light spoilers as it is, but let's give you a score out of ten from me:
9.75/10

TLDR; Cool concept, for a pretty niche community. Unfortnately there's no singleplayer mode and finding other players can take upwards of 10 minutes. Controls can feel unresponsive, but gameplay is genuinely fun. Online community feels dead and the game lacks varitey and customisability.
I imagine they'd also be rolling out more updates in the future for more content, as it is there are 6 tracks and 6 different cars. When you start out you have no cars theres 6 to pick from and you have a choice of the first two as they are under 200K which is what you're given when you start out. The car models do look pretty good and was impressed with the details they were able to put into the models. After buying the car you want, take it to your garage and with whatever spare cash you have left you might be able to get an upgrade. The upgradeable aspects of your car are the brake, ECU, Exhaust, bodywork, suspension, KERS, spoiler, cooling and a few others. Upgrades will change the car in terms of fuel economy, top speed, accleration, drag, braking power and do matter. For instance the car I was using was kitted to last only about 25km's without pitting but I had constantly more power to use and ended out on top. Most races won't be longer than 50km's, also note drivers can be more fuel economic whilst driving.
Once you're actually in-game it's pretty fun, you instruct your AI driver around and tell him when to use KERS, push harder, when to change the car's fuel map, pitstops and block. Controls can feel like they are unresponsive at times but that's due to driver stats which can be upgrades with experience points.
Experience points can be used to increase the speed of certain aspects of your pitstop, increase the skill of your driver; how confident he is with braking and overtaking and how much speed he can carry through corners. You also have a manager who handles all your sponsorship contracts, you can give him greater chance of securing a contract and he can land better contracts for you aswell.
Contracts themselves aren't overly fun to handle. You're given 10 time units and every action uses a certain amount of time units, time units are replentished after each race. Pretty easy mechanic but monotonous is a good way to describe sponsorship (10/10 immersion there). To actually land a deal you need to call up the sponsor which you might or might not get through to. Once you're in you can invite them out to dinner, send them gifts, give a presentation on your raceteam few other options I've forgotten. Each option will better the relationship between you and whomever you're chasing up.
Once a you manage to squeeze out a contract offer you can change the aspects of the contract, how much you get paid, for how many races and what position you need to come in to adhere to those conditions of receiving the funds.
All up I would recommend this game if they added more varitey and the online community was bigger, it's a fairly niche market so this game may never live up to it's full potential. In it's current state I wouldn't recommend this game.
Apologies for the length of the review, it all got a bit out of hand. Cheers.

An extremely fun little action rpg with good combat, and robust customization that allows you to not only edit your characters stats and abilities in depth, but even their appearance pixel by pixel.
Control and combat wise, it's a top down action rpg, similar to Legend of Zelda visually and control wise. You can jump, you can block, you can slide, and you got a variety of abilities and weapon types at your disposal. There's even a decent amount of finesse and tricks you can do, like cancelling sword slashes into blockings and then jumping out of danger to save yourself, or buffering jumps into short jumping attacks.
The enemies you face also have nice variety, and do a good job of remaining fairly unpredictable even after you've learned their fighting styles. Another thing I especially love, is that the game incorporates a subtle stealth element. Enemies won't start chasing and attacking you till they spot you, but once they do they'll chase you through the entire dungeon. Attempting to run from an enemy will cause you to rush by other enemies, who will also break into chase. This results in a frantic chase through the entire dungeon as you attempt to escape in time from the horde trying to corner you.
For customization, you're allowed to create as many characters as you like, selecting jobs, weapons, and abilities. You strengthen their abilities and growth in certain areas by drawing on the strength of other characters you've created. Visually, you can edit weapons and characters (and even animation) of your characters pixel by pixel. Don't be daunted though, because the game uses a great template for creating fairly basic but still cute looking sprites. More artistic players can still create some great stuff though.
The actual gameplay is basically divided into two games. You can make your way through the static progression of dungeons of the main campaign, which has decent level/dungeon design and is balanced well enough to not require any grinding. Alternatively, you can take on a massive 100 floor randomly generated dungeon, which feels more like a rogue like.
I personally love the randomly generated dungeon, the way stealth, combat, traps, and preparation are balanced is fantastic. Unfortunately, enemies increase in level ridiculously fast as you proceed through the floors. Eventually your attacks will do 0 damage, so it's really quite impossible to clear the dungeon based on skill alone. While making it as far as you can and escaping with random rare loot (you lose everything if you die before making it to an exit), is plenty exciting and skillbased, it's still ultimately a long term process to clear it the entire dungeon itself.
ClaDun X2 is still a fantastic game, plenty fun, and allows you to play and create your characters to suit your needs. I would highly recommend it for some hack and slash fun.

I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys figuring out if someone is lying. In this game you are randomly assigned a role which can range from a town member with a unique ability to a mafia member with the goal of killing town members, or to a neutral character whose goal is to create chaos. There are day and night cycles; during the day you are free to chat and try to figure out the bad guys. At night, you  perform your special ability which can range from killing someone, investigating, or channeling the dead. It is always a thrill at the end of the night when you find out if you lived or died. The real fun for serious players is located in ranked mode which requires 50 games played in other modes to unlock. There are always some bad apples in the game who are negative/salty or not being true to their role, but the in-game reporting system allows the developers to take care of these people by banning them. You can buy cosmetic items like houses and characters with in-game currency that is earned by playing games or with real money. All the items are purely cosmetic and do not affect gameplay at all. I wouldn't recommend paying real money since it seems like you get so little in return for your money; the town points aren't cheap. The game is being actively improved as new roles are coming to the game in the future. Overall this is an exciting casual game to play in your down time.
